meta.title: Save in Swiss francs and earn the protocol rate | Frankencoin
meta.description: Deposit ZCHF, the decentralized Swiss franc, in the savings module and earn the rate set by governance. Withdraw any time. Live rate and three steps to start.

hero.title: Swiss francs that|earn {rate} a year.
hero.subtitle: ZCHF is a Swiss franc on public blockchains. Deposit it in the savings module and it earns the protocol rate; withdraw whenever you like.

how.title: Where the interest comes from
how.body: Borrowers lock collateral, mint ZCHF and pay interest into the protocol. The savings module pays savers the rate set by Frankencoin governance out of that income. Interest accrues continuously once it starts and is withdrawn together with your deposit, in one transaction, whenever you want.

steps.title: Start in three steps
steps.subtitle: Already hold ZCHF? Go straight to step 3. Holding ZCHF in a wallet earns nothing; interest is paid only on what you deposit in the savings module.

items.title: Get ZCHF
items.body: Bank transfer in CHF or EUR via Mt Pelerin (0% fees), or swap from USDC, USDT or ETH on any DEX.

items.title: Connect a wallet
items.body: Open the savings page in the app with any Ethereum wallet. Savings run on Ethereum and seven other chains.

items.title: Deposit into savings
items.body: One transaction. Interest starts three days after the deposit and then accrues continuously. If a wallet or app set itself as referrer, its share (up to 25% of your interest) is deducted and shown in the app.

alt.text: Prefer a token you can trade or use as collateral while it earns? The Savings Vault (svZCHF) is an alternative.
alt.label: About svZCHF

faq.q: I already hold ZCHF. Am I earning interest?
faq.a: Not yet. ZCHF in a wallet earns nothing. Deposit it in the [savings module](https://app.frankencoin.com/savings); interest starts three days later.
Yes. Your deposit and the interest it earned can be withdrawn whenever you want, with no notice period.

faq.q: Who sets the rate, and can it change?
faq.a: Frankencoin governance (FCS holders) sets the rate and can change it. The current rate is shown at the top of this page and in the app.

faq.q: Is anything deducted from the interest?
faq.a: The protocol charges no fee. If you deposited through a wallet or app that set itself as referrer, up to 25% of your interest goes to it. The app shows the referrer and the share, and you can remove it.

cta.title: Swiss francs that earn interest.
cta.body: Deposit ZCHF once, withdraw whenever you like.

tbills.title: Why not just buy T-bills?|Because the yield is in dollars.
tbills.subtitle: Treasury bills are the classic safe dollar. Here is what {amount} did since {year}: rolled into 3-month T-bills every quarter, against the same money changed into francs and left at Swiss cash rates.

chf.label: {amount} changed into francs in {year}
chf.note: {chf} then, earning Swiss cash rates, changed back to dollars today.

tbills.need: Needed just to keep up with US inflation: {need}

reasons.title: The yield did not offset the currency.
reasons.body: T-bills paid {tbillAvg} a year on average since {year}. The dollar lost {fxLoss} against the franc over the same period, which more than offset the higher yield.

reasons.title: A 6% dollar is roughly a 3% franc
reasons.body: The forward market prices the expected currency drift into the rate gap, so a high dollar yield and a lower franc yield tend to land in the same place. With ZCHF the {rate} is paid in francs, without currency risk against the franc.

reasons.title: No broker, no US account, no settlement days
reasons.body: T-bills need a brokerage or TreasuryDirect and, for non-Americans, tax paperwork. ZCHF needs a wallet: deposit in one transaction, interest accrues daily, withdraw any time.

reasons.title: Backed by collateral you can inspect
reasons.body: A T-bill is a government's promise. ZCHF is backed by over-collateralized loans you can inspect on-chain at any time. Check the live figures on the Transparency page.

tbills.source: Annual averages from FRED: 3-month Treasury bill TB3MS, H.10 exchange rates, BLS CPI-U; Swiss cash rates from the SNB (call money to 1998, SARON from 1999). Returns ignore taxes and fees. Past moves do not predict future ones; ZCHF carries smart-contract and collateral risk.
